create.title: Hard-TOP t=1 residual maximal parity-Fejer positive-transform obstruction
create.statement_tex: Let J=sqrt(X), 1<<L<<H<=J^(1/2), R_0=ceil(L), M asymp L^2, and retain the complete literal residual sequence z_N=c_N^rem e(Jsqrt(N)), zero-extended on an M-site containing interval, with D_L=sum_N|z_N|^2<<_epsilon L^2X^epsilon. The exact even parity-Fejer stopped chain writes (165.K26) as one half of the adjacent-scale energy increments minus one O_epsilon(L^3X^epsilon) short correction. For every integer R<S<=2R the link weight is b_(R,S)(r)=r(S-R)/(RS) for 0<r<R, 1-r/S for R<=r<S, and 0 for r>=S, with b_(R,S)(0)=0; exact doublings have the absolute-site-parity Haar identity and a strict terminal link uses this Fejer difference. The first link is O_epsilon(L^3X^epsilon) but has no target-safe complement. A real disjoint-cardinal interpolation gives the exact common-frequency transform Z_epsilon(theta)=(i/2) sum_(k odd)chi_4(k) sum_ell Btilde_(epsilon,theta)(k/4,ell), and the squared parity-averaged link has coefficient 1/8 with one outer real part. All terms with ell=0 or ell'=0 are O_epsilon(L^3X^epsilon) only after every signed odd character frequency is recombined. The complete signed ell,ell' nonzero aggregate remains open. The physical zero diagonal is not a zero dual diagonal; cancellation occurs only after all dual, cell, endpoint, transition, and zero-extension pieces recombine. Any continuation that, before a proved literal actual-symbol saving, replaces this signed family by a coefficient-uniform positive norm over modes, cells, openings, or common frequency has available maximal-link scale MD_L<<_epsilon L^4X^epsilon. On an admissible M=4P stopped-chain subfamily, a nonliteral dechirped one-parity array attains MD_L/8 asymp L^4. At either centred peak a smooth-interior fixed lawful opening returns to the accepted rank-one product collar. This is a scoped no-go only for coefficient-uniform positivity before an actual-symbol gain. It does not exclude cross-link cancellation or a coefficient-sensitive literal positive theorem, is not physical lower mass, and neither proves nor disproves (165.K26).
